To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the representation of Captain Maria LaGuerta is progressive in that it breaks down racial and gender boundaries by depicting a Latina in a high position of power, and (2) the co construction of Latinidad online reproduces stereotypical representations of Latinas as sexualized and hyperfeminine, and as immigrants.

(1) the Latina character Maria LaGuerta in Dexter, while a breakthrough role for Latina representation in the media, is still limited in her portrayal as a strong and independent Latina woman, (2) the audience co constructions of Maria LaGuerta as a Latina in the media are limited to a few stereotypical images, and (3) the audience co construction of Maria LaGuertas Latina identity is based on the notion of a Latina as being a woman of color and an immigrant, and
the character of Captain Maria LaGuerta in the television series Dexter is a progressive representation of Latinas, and that this representation is not reproduced by the audience.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which audiences construct and negotiate meanings about the representation of Latinidad in media.
how audiences co construct meanings and identities in relation to the media text.

how Latinas are constructed and consumed in the media, how the representation and consumption of these characters is related to current racial discourses in the United States, and the ideological effects of such constructions and readings on Latinidad and Latinas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, although the character of LaGuerta is a positive representation of a Latina, it is a stereotypical representation of a Latina.
the representation of the Latina character Maria LaGuerta on Showtime's Dexter is an ambivalent representation that is both progressive and conservative.
the representation of a Latina Captain on Dexter does not break down stereotypical representations of Latinidad.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this thesis is a study of a Latina character's representation in a popular television show, and an analysis of the ways in which the character is interpreted by audiences.
the representation of a Latina character as a "breakthrough" role in a mainstream television show is not necessarily a positive development for the representation of Latina/o identity in the media.

the representation of Captain Maria LaGuerta as a "progressive" Latina in Showtime's series, Dexter, does not break with the reproduction of stereotyped representations of Latinidad based in homogeneity, symbolic colonialism, and immigration as a marker of Latinidad.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, while the media industry is increasingly producing and distributing more diverse and inclusive representations, these representations do not necessarily reflect the complexity and diversity of contemporary racial and gendered identities.

the audience co construction of Latinidad is not only shaped by the media text but also by a complex set of social factors, which include the racialization of Latinidad in the U.S., the racialization of Latina/o audiences, and the racialization of the Internet as a medium.

the audience co construction of the character Maria LaGuerta is a complex process that involves the interplay of multiple discourses on Latinidades and the negotiation of multiple identities and subject positions by viewers online.
